Porsche's Panamera Is Getting a Facelift Less Than 3 Years After Its Debut
23 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
The current Porsche Panamera is in the third generation, with the official unveiling taking pace toward the end of 2023. The model hit the assembly line the following year, and even though it is still very young, the Zuffenhausen-based auto mark has decided to prepare its mid-cycle refresh.
We have seen the facelifted Panamera on a few occasions, and the model has just ended up under the spotlight yet again courtesy of our spy photographers, who recently mailed us the scoops you see above. These show another prototype of the upcoming machine that takes on the infamous Nurburgring racetrack in Germany. And from what we can tell, we are likely looking at the Panamera GTS.
Why do we believe that? Because the tester in question features four round tailpipes at the rear, as well as centerlock wheels. This prototype did not have much camouflage on its body, as the team behind it probably thought that it would allow the car to fly under the radar. Little did they know that they cannot trick our man with the cam, who was ready to immortalize it from several angles as it drove by.
From what we can tell, the facelifted Porsche Panamera has only a few updates here and there, and we definitely need a side-by-side comparison with the current GTS to tell what’s new. The front bumper is part of the novelties, as it features diagonal slats on the side vents instead of the outgoing one’s horizontal slats, as well as a reworked central section. The headlights have some tape on the outer edges, and they have likely been tweaked for the mid-cycle refresh.
Photo: SH Proshots The profile holds nothing new for the time being, as the wheels are identical to those of the current Porsche Panamera GTS. However, we expect this aspect to change once the facelifted one goes official, and chances are that we could also be looking at a revised color palette. Out back, we can see that this prototype featured a different bumper with a slightly more aggressive design. The diffuser should also be new, and the taillights will likely be tweaked.
Thus, it is an evolutionary update rather than a revolutionary one, and some automakers could learn a few things from this. And that’s something strange to say about Porsche, because the company’s designs have always been considered a bit lazy, but seeing what’s going on in today’s automotive world, we, or I in this case, have started appreciating what the Zuffenhausen brand does. And chances are you may agree. So, do you?
Before inviting you to scroll down and reveal your impressions on the facelifted Porsche Panamera , we also have to talk you though other aspects. For instance, it will feature a new center console on the inside, and chances are the physical controls for the HVAC system will be replaced with a touchscreen display. A new digital gauge cluster, and a slightly revised dashboard panel will likely be part of the makeover, alongside perhaps the steering wheel.
Word on the street is that the powertrain family could be updated in order to help it meet the stricter Euro 7 emission regulations on the right side of the pond. It is yet unknown if these changes will bring more power to the table, as that’s a question that will be answered in due course. Meanwhile, we will remind you that the current Panamera is offered in seven different versions in our market.
Photo: SH Proshots The base flavor of the car is simply called the Porsche Panamera , and has an MSRP of $113,000 for the latest model year, enjoying 348 horsepower (353 ps/260 kW) from its 2.9-liter six-cylinder engine with twin turbocharging, and it hits 60 mph (97 kph) in 4.8 seconds, tapping out at 169 mph (272 kph). The Panamera 4 follows with the same output, 0-60 mph in 4.7 seconds, and an MSRP of $120,400.
Next comes the electrified Porsche Panamera 4 E-Hybrid, with its 463-horsepower powertrain, the ability to hit 60 mph in 3.9 seconds with the Sport Chrono Package, and a starting price of $127,700. The Panamera 4S E-Hybrid has 536 horsepower on tap, can complete the sprint in as little as 3.5 seconds, and kicks off at $139,100. The GTS has 493 hp, is one-tenth of a second slower than the 4S E-Hybrid, and starts at $166,900.
For the current Porsche Panamera Turbo E-Hybrid , one must prepare a minimum of $207,900 (MSRP). This model has 670 horsepower to play with, and hits 60 mph in just 3.0 seconds. Sitting at the top of the family is the Panamera Turbo S E-Hybrid, with its 771 horsepower combined, 0-60 mph in 2.8 seconds, and a starting price of $245,200.
Chances are the facelifted Porsche Panamera will become a bit more expensive compared to the current one, and we expect it to premiere in the coming months, probably arriving at dealers nationwide for the 2028 model year. Now, what’s your take on the model’s mid-cycle refresh?

Porsche Mission S: This Is What the New Hypercar Concept Will Look Like – Rendering
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | avarvarii
After a long wait, Porsche is finally ready to launch a new hypercar, and it being previewed by the Mission S Concept that will be unveiled a few hours from now.
Following in the footsteps of the iconic Porsche 918 Spyder, the Mission S recently leaked in all its glory, and that short video has been used by @avarvarii to create a set of very realistic renderings. The digital illustrations shared above reveal how the upcoming model will look, and we have to admit that it is unlike anything we have seen from the Zuffenhausen brand, at least when it comes to the styling of the back end.
In fact, these CGIs focus solely on the car’s rear end, as it spilled the beans on its design from this angle. We can see that the fat rear three-quarter panels blend in with the bumper and diffuser on the lower part of the body, and with the integrated wing on the deck. The taillights are very slim, and “ Mission ” emblem sits between them. Further down, we can see a rather discreet diffuser, and cutouts for the vertically stacked quad exhaust tips.
It also features rear glass panels similar to those of the Bugatti Chiron, to some extent, obviously, and we can also see that the engine cover has a fan mounted on top of it. And that sends Porsche 917 vibes. The Mission S Concept has a vented hood at the front, extremely muscular front fenders, sharp-looking side skirts, traditional door mirrors, and it looks ready to give other supercars a headache. Let’s just hope that the final product looks this cool.
Photo: Instagram | avarvarii Previous reports indicated that the Mission S might draw some inspiration from the Porsche Mission X Concept unveiled in 2023, but from what we can tell, it does not have anything in common with that show car. The new study is part of the company’s 35 plan detailed recently by the company’s head honcho, Michael Leiters. And in case you missed it, you should know that the automaker is struggling financially, and believes that making fewer cars and scoring a huge profit on each one is the key to success.
That is where the Porsche Mission S comes in, as it gives us a first look at “ a potential mid-engine super sports car platform for the future. ” That is pretty much everything we know about it so far. Well, that and the design of the back end that has recently leaked in all its glory, hours before the model’s official premiere. Nevertheless, it is logical to assume that the hypercar will sit well above the 911 series, which costs upward of $135,500 for the base Carrera and reaches almost $300,000 when it comes to the Turbo S .
It is safe to say that the production model will be aimed at enthusiasts with very deep pockets. Reports indicate that it will be priced at well over half a million dollars, though some believe that it could end up costing as much as $1.5 million. Or maybe even more. And the model won’t only follow in the footsteps of the 918 Spyder, but also the Carrera GT.
The latter model was made in 1,270 examples at the Leipzig factory in Germany between 2003 and 2006. It was a two-door Targa roadster with a longitudinally mounted rear mid-engine and rear-wheel drive layout. Power came from a 5.7-liter V10. The mill was good for 603 horsepower (612 0s/450 kW) and 435 pound-feet (590 Nm) of torque, channeled to the wheels through a six-speed manual transmission. It dealt with 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) in 3.9 seconds, and maxed out at 205 mph (330 kph).
Photo: Instagram | avarvarii Its successor, the Porsche 918 Spyder, was assembled at the Zuffenhausen facility in Stuttgart, Germany, between 2013 and 2015. As its name implies, it is an open-top model (Targa), and it boasts electrified firepower. Two electric motors mounted on the front and rear axles assist the 4.6-liter V8 engine, kicking out a total system output of 875 hp (887 ps/652 kW) and 944 pound-feet (1,280 Nm) of torque.
Taking on the likes of the McLaren P1 and the Ferrari LaFerrari, the Porsche 918 hit 62 mph (100 kph) in as little as 2.6 seconds with the Weissach Package installed, and could keep pushing all the way up to 214 mph (345 kph).
Usually, a Porsche 918 Spyder will set you back between over $2 million and more than $4 million in today’s used car market in the United States of America, and it is worth noting that one recently sold for more than $6 million. As for its predecessor, the Carrera GT, it tends to change hands from $1.5 million to $4.5 million, though in rare cases, this model can fetch well over $6 million.
So, are you excited about Porsche launching a successor to the Carrera GT and the 918? Do you like the way the Mission S looks? Tell us all about it in the comments area below. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Avarvarii Automotive Artworks (@avarvarii)

Audi's Hottest Electric Wagon Yet Shows Wider Arches, Might Not Be Called RS6 Avant e-tron
14 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
Ingolstadt is currently putting the finishing touches on a high-performance longroof with all-electric propulsion instead of a hybridized V8. Originally believed to be christened RS 6 Avant e-tron, the newcomer may be called something different.
Per insider sources cited by Top Gear back in September 2025, the RS 6 e-tron project was canceled, leaving the S6 e-tron as the flagship. Audi reportedly decided on this due to dismally low projected sales. Furthermore, the RS treatment would also jeopardize the already struggling RS e-tron GT.
Having cleared that up, hearsay suggests S6 e-tron performance as the name of this version. To be offered in both sedan and wagon flavors, the all-wheel-drive bruiser definitely looks more purposeful compared to the non-performance S6 e-tron. Spied near the most demanding circuit in the world, the Avant-bodied prototype sits lower and is definitely wider where it actually matters.
The heavily flared wheel arches are complemented by vertical openings beside the front doors, namely vents that improve airflow along the bodysides while also reducing front-end aerodynamic lift by relieving the high-pressure air that builds up inside the wheel wells. Trapped air creates high-pressure zones that act against the underside of the fenders, pushing the front of the car upward.
Its face carries the split-headlight setup and covered Singleframe grille of the S6 e-tron, yet the front bumper makes it a Performance model. Redesigned intakes are on the menu, along with a more prominent splitter designed to better manage airflow at high speeds and under spirited cornering.
Photo: SH Proshots Moving along its flanks, large alloys with a diamond-cut finish and six double spokes appear to be intended for series production. The side skirts nicely tie the more aggressive front end into the backside, giving the S6 e-tron Performance a more planted silhouette. At the rear, changes include a slightly different roof spoiler and a larger aerodynamic diffuser that looks better integrated into the bumper than the diffuser of the S6 e-tron.
Look closer, and you will further notice upgraded brakes that definitely make sense on a car that carries a bigger punch and more purposeful aero. Regarding that bigger punch, it's worth remembering that Audi lists the S6 e-tron with 543 horsepower in launch mode and no more than 631 pound-feet (855 Newton-meters) of twist from dual electric drive units.
The S6 Avant e-tron requires 3.9 seconds to hit 100 kilometers per hour, onto a top speed of 240 kilometers per hour. In American speak, those would be 3.7 seconds to 60 miles per hour and 149 miles an hour on the right tires. Because of the wider body and downforce-favoring updates, the S6 e-tron Performance may not match the maximum speed of the S6 e-tron.
Beyond the aforementioned goodies, the Performance version may also come with a sportier interior. More bolstering for the front seats and carbon-fiber trim would be great differentiators that would cost Audi little in the way of R&D money. Considering that S6 e-tron Performance designates a step below the stillborn RS 6 e-tron, one has to wonder how many of these will actually be sold in the first year of production.

Bell MV-75 Cheyenne II Black Hawk Replacement Moves Closer to First Test Flight
21 photos
Photo: Bell
Based on what American defense contractor Bell Textron and the U.S. Army have been saying over the past year or so, I was kind of expecting the first flight of the MV-75 Cheyenne II tiltrotor to take place by the end of this year. Yet, judging by what Bell said earlier this week, that’s highly unlikely.
After it said it completed the first two wing structures for the first two test examples of the aircraft earlier this June, the defense contractor revealed that a number of the design’s most important components are now ready.
That includes the completion of the first nacelles that are meant to hold Rolls-Royce AE 1107F turboshaft engines – the same kind that is also deployed on the Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules and the V-22 Osprey.
As soon as that happened, engineers set out to integrate the nacelles with the wings and successfully completed that task as well. At the same time, the company says it began testing the gearboxes that are meant to power several of the aircraft’s components, including the electrical power generators, hydraulic pumps, and cooling blowers for the engine and nacelle.
Other teams are working on getting other major components and systems ready for duty, including the flight control computers, general-purpose computers, actuator drive unit, electrical components, and large area displays.
When ready for duty, the MV-75 Cheyenne II will slowly but surely replace the aging UH-60 Black Hawk in the Army’s arsenal, promising to deliver twice the speed and twice the range of the iconic helicopter.
In numbers we can all understand, that would be a top speed of 345 mph (555 kph) and a maximum distance that can be reached on a single fill of the tanks of 575 miles (925 km). Partially responsible for that is the fact that the Cheyenne can lift off and land just like a helicopter, while traveling through the air like a conventional fixed-wing aircraft. The tiltrotor will be capable of transporting 12 soldiers and 12,000 pounds (5.4 tons) of cargo.
The Cheyenne is the winner of the Army’s Future Long Range Assault Aircraft (FLRAA) program, and it was first referred to as the V-280 Valor. Despite being significantly different from the helicopter it is meant to replace, it will pretty much be used in the same (and many) roles: troop insertion, medevac, long-range air assault operations, and disaster relief, among others.
It’s unclear how many of these tiltrotors will eventually deploy, but if we are to judge by the size of the Black Hawk fleet, we’re probably talking about thousands of them. Each Cheyenne is expected to cost the Army at least $43 million, about double the cost of the Black Hawk currently in use.

Blue Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 Races Older BMW M4 and Brand-New M2, Someone Gets Rolled at 165 MPH
17 photos
Photo: Import 2 Race / YouTube
It seems like we've been waiting forever for a resolution, as this is really getting long in the tooth: it’s already been a decidedly long time since the good folks over at the racing-focused ' Import 2 Race ' channel on YouTube have returned to their traditional venue - Island Dragway in Great Meadows, New Jersey. Instead, they’re passionate about roll races instead of quarter-mile dragstrip skirmishes, apparently.
So, they remain firmly focused on 65-mph roll race battles – this time around between a blue sixth-generation Chevrolet Camaro ZL1, which is powered by the iconic 6.2-liter LT4 supercharged V8 engine and packs 650 hp and 650 lb-ft of torque, and a couple of Bavarians. Those are of the BMW M4 and M2 variety, albeit they come from different periods in time.
Thus, probably enticed by something else other than the countless prepped surface quarter-mile battles they have witnessed over the years, the videographer keeps dwelling around a place where time isn’t of the essence, and instead we focus on high-speed ‘drama’: the legendary Pocono Raceway , a 2.5-mile tri-oval track in Blakeslee, Pennsylvania.
Around since 1969, this place has seen just about everything, including a massive lineup of events from NASCAR, the IndyCar Series, and the IMSA GT Championship series, along with much smaller gatherings that are nevertheless quite interesting, like RaceMotive’s 65-mph roll race series. So, while we wait for brand-new quarter-mile dragstrip battles, the videographer continues to capture footage of high-speed clashes between models like the Chevy Camaro and the BMW M4 or M2.
The first skirmish is between the Camaro ZL1 and a silver BMW M4 of the F82 variety, aka the generation without humongous kidney grilles. It looked feisty and ready for action with the black aerodynamic package and blue-painted brake calipers, but as it turns out the Chevrolet didn’t even have to worry itself about the outcome: 157 mph versus just 137 mph for the Bavarian coupe.
Quite shameful, indeed. Luckily, there was a second battle against a contemporary BMW M2 of the G87 variety, all black and menacing save for the red brake calipers. It even had a swan-neck rear wing of the aftermarket variety, which added to the visual thrills, plus concave Y-spoke alloy wheels. Well, we can’t say it was all show and no go because the little rascal produced in Mexico that uses the same 3.0-liter S58 twin-turbo inline-six as the BMW M3 topped out at 138 mph.
But it was certainly nowhere near enough to catch up to the Camaro ZL1, which upped the stakes according to the threat next to it and delivered a smashing victory at over 165 mph! So, what do you think? Should the Chevy Camaro come back with a seventh generation and provide additional high-speed and quarter-mile thrills or not?

The Only 2004 Mercedes-Benz CLK DTM AMG Owned by F1 Champion Jenson Button Could Sell for $660K
12 photos
Photo: Iconic Auctioneers
German carmaker Mercedes-Benz is not one to release special, limited-edition versions of its cars all that often. This reality makes such vehicles released in the past worth a lot of money. Especially when one of them has a long connection with a former Formula 1 champion.
The car I’m talking about is something called the Mercedes-Benz CLK DTM AMG , a special vehicle that was in production in the mid-2000s as a means for the German carmaker to celebrate its undisputed dominance in the Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters (DTM) at the time.
The model, inspired by the championship-winning competition car driven in DTM, was put together with help from the same guys who ran the works cars in the racing series, HWA AG. Only 100 of them were ever made, each powered by a supercharged 5.4-litre V8 engine that cranked out 574 horsepower and could hit 62 mph from a standstill in 3.9 seconds, on its way to a top speed of 199 mph (320 kph).
As soon as it was made, one of the CLK DTM AMG cars, a 2004 example, was delivered to F1 driver Jenson Button. The man seems to have really liked the car, as he kept on to it for 15 years. Granted, he didn’t drive it all that much during this time, as the vehicle shows only a little over 18,100 miles (11,300 km) of use.
Button let go of the car in 2019, when it was sold to a Japanese collector. It is that buyer who will now be letting go of the car as well, during the Iconic Auctioneers sale at the NEC Classic Motor Show in the UK in mid-November.
Presently in stock form, with its carbon-fiber bodywork, distinct flared arches, large wing at the rear, and the two-seat interior with motorsport influences, the 2004 Mercedes-Benz CLK DTM AMG is selling with a lot of accompanying paperwork, including servicing papers from before being sold to the Japanese, with the Guernsey Registration Certificate in Jenson Button's name, and documentation confirming its technical specification.
Also thrown in the package are the original CLK DTM owner's wallet, two keys, complete tool kit, tire compressor, oil filter, and first aid kit.
That’s the full package, if you will, but probably not what makes this car worth an estimated £500,000 (about $663,000 at today’s exchange rates). What makes it so is that it was owned by Button for most of his F1 career, from his early days at BAR-Honda to his move to McLaren late in his career.
In between, the car was in the driver’s possession when he won the World Championship in the colors of Brawn GP.
I will keep an eye on the Jenson Button-owned 2004 Mercedes-Benz CLK DTM AMG and report back once I learn how much it went for.

Mercedes-Benz GLE 450 e 4Matic SUV and Coupe Heads to Land Down Under With PHEV For the First Time
24 photos
Photo: Mercedes-Benz
The premium German automaker's Australian division has announced a new addition to the Mercedes-Benz GLE roster, the first plug-in hybrid addition to the family: the GLE 450 e 4Matic with both SUV and Coupe body styles.
On an international level, Mercedes is preoccupied with announcing that the renowned Mercedes-Maybach S-Class individualized by LeBron James through Manufaktur Made to Measure is heading to auction for a good cause. A near-identical twin to LeBron James’ personal Maybach S-Class will be offered through Gooding & Christie’s at Retromobile New York in November, with proceeds from the auction to benefit the LeBron James Family Foundation and its ‘I Promise’ program.
But over in the Land Down Under, Mercedes-Benz Australia has more prosaic news: in September they announced the Mercedes-AMG G 63 Two-Finish Edition, the opening of Mercedes-Benz Studio Sydney, the facelifted EQS Sedan, the new launch of the premium transfer service with Qantas, as well as the all-new GLB compact crossover SUV, and now they finally have something fresh for October, too.
So, meet the Australian versions of the new Mercedes-Benz GLE 450 e 4Matic plug-in hybrid SUV and Coupe models which “bring electrified performance to the GLE range.” They combined a 3.0-liter inline-six gasoline engine with electric driving thanks to a 135 kW (181 hp) PSM electric motor. The combined output is 320 kW and 680 Nm, or 429 hp and 502 lb-ft of torque, and power delivery is through standard all-wheel drive and a 9G-Tronic automatic transmission.
Most importantly, the new model also has a 25.7 kWh usable high-voltage battery, so the GLE 450 e features a WLTP-tested electric range of 87 km for the SUV and 91 km for the Coupe, which is 54 and 57 miles, respectively. Electric driving can happen at up to 140 kph or 87 mph, which means that both “shorter everyday trips and freeway journeys can be completed without the petrol engine.”
The Mercedes-Benz GLE 450 e 4Matic plug-in hybrid model has all the goodies introduced with the recent mid-cycle refresh of the model family, and this version comes with standard 20-inch AMG five-spoke alloys for the SUV and 21-inch AMG five-twin-spoke rims for the Coupe. AMG Line exterior styling and the Night Package also come standard on the GLE 450 e.
Moving inside, the PHEV model gets heated front seats and an Artico man-made leather interior trim, a standard AMG Line Sport Seats Package upholstered in Artico with Microcut microfiber inserts in black, the MBUX Superscreen with three 12.3-inch displays tucked under a single glass surface, and the Mercedes‑Benz Operating System (MB.OS) with over-the-air updates.
Pricing kicks off at AU$156,900 (MRLP) and AU$160,900 (MRLP), for the SUV and Coupe, respectively. That’s almost $109k and over $111k at the current exchange rate, by the way.

Counter-drone systems can combine radar, cameras, radio-frequency sensors and other equipment to detect, track and identify potential threats. Honeywell Aerospace’s SAMURAI system is designed to bring information from those disparate sources into a single interface.
The system uses UNITAS , Honeywell Aerospace’s battle-management software, to integrate sensors and effectors from different manufacturers.
“There is no one solution that solves every threat out there,” said retired Air Force Col. Tom Konicki, director of business at Honeywell Aerospace.
The threat ranges from recreational drones flown into restricted airspace to unmanned aircraft that could be used to attack military installations or other critical infrastructure. Konicki said counter-drone systems need to detect, track, identify, classify and ultimately defeat drones, regardless of the operator’s intent.
“The threat is real, and the threat is now,” he added.
While SAMURAI stands for Stationary and Mobile UAS Reveal and Intercept, UNITAS is not an acronym. Konicki said the name was inspired by football player Johnny Unitas.
Counter-drone systems can combine several types of equipment. Radar detects objects at a distance, while radio-frequency sensors can detect signals associated with drones or their controllers. Remote identification equipment can receive identifying information broadcast by compliant drones. Electro-optical and infrared cameras allow operators to examine objects more closely, while acoustic sensors can help detect drones by their sound.
Depending on the threat and equipment available, counter-drone systems can also use electronic warfare, directed-energy systems, conventional weapons or interceptor drones to defeat an aircraft. Some systems use nets to capture drones, an approach that can be designed to reduce the risk of debris falling onto people or property.
Konicki said operators of some counter-drone systems must monitor six, seven or eight separate screens for radar, cameras, radio-frequency sensors, jamming equipment and other capabilities. That can require one operator to track multiple information streams simultaneously. UNITAS is designed to consolidate the feeds so operators can view information from multiple sensors together in one interface.
“We call it a single pane of glass,” Konicki said. “There could be seven different sensors that have identified it and are feeding that into our software.”
Konicki said the interface is designed to be straightforward for operators, including younger service members who may be assigned counter-drone duties without extensive experience operating the different systems. He said Honeywell Aerospace has demonstrated the software to U.S. government and military representatives, as well as local law enforcement and state and city representatives.
The software also uses an open-architecture approach, allowing customers to integrate equipment they already own instead of replacing it with products from a single manufacturer.
“We’re not asking them to go buy new stuff,” Konicki said. “We can integrate with what they already have.”
Customers can choose equipment suited to their needs and update components as detection technologies and countermeasures evolve. Konicki said Honeywell Aerospace works with other companies to incorporate their technologies rather than lock customers into a single vendor’s products. He said the company seeks equipment mature enough for operational use rather than untested technology.
At the Association of the United States Army’s annual meeting, Honeywell Aerospace displayed a mockup of the mobile configuration mounted on the back of a Ford F-150. Konicki called it the “Green Beast.”
Honeywell Aerospace is also developing an airborne application of SAMURAI with Odys Aviation. Announced in March 2026, the collaboration aims to adapt the system for Odys’ long-range Laila uncrewed aircraft. The companies said the effort builds on more than a year of joint development and systems-integration work. Laila is intended to be the first airborne application of SAMURAI, extending the system beyond ground-based and mobile configurations.
Konicki said SAMURAI can also be configured for fixed-site protection and maritime operations. Depending on the mission, customers might position equipment around a building or installation, use a mobile configuration for temporary protection at an event, or place sensors at distributed locations to cover a larger area.
Separately, Honeywell Aerospace announced Oct. 12 that its wholly owned subsidiary, EMS Defense Technologies, was selected for a Department of Homeland Security counter-drone contract vehicle . The five-year, multiple-award vehicle has a $1.5 billion ceiling, was awarded July 31 and took effect Aug. 1.
Konicki said Honeywell Aerospace works with international partners, including Lithuania, Slovakia and Colombia, and can integrate locally sourced equipment when customers want to use particular sensors or effectors.
For customers protecting an air base or another site, Konicki said the company can assess where radar, cameras and other sensors should be positioned to maximize coverage.
Its planning process can map areas with adequate coverage, identify gaps and recommend adjustments to equipment placement. The company can then conduct what Konicki described as a red-team assessment, examining where an adversary might launch a drone and how that approach could affect the site’s defenses. The analysis will help customers tailor sensor placement and other system components to the site and its potential threats.

Xiaomi's Upcoming SU7 Ultra Extreme Dons Revised Aerodynamics in Latest Spy Photos
17 photos
Photo: Baldauf
Xiaomi is refining the SU7 Ultra Extreme formula, and the latest pair of prototypes the carparazzi spotted at the Nurburgring shows a great deal of changes from previous test vehicles. The emphasis here is aerodynamics, and the focus is downforce generation with minimal drag penalties.
The most obvious change sits out back, where the wing shows a twin-plane design and swan-neck supports. A drag reduction system is likely featured, especially when you remember that swan-neck supports can easily accommodate the linkages that make DRS plausible. Rather crazy on an electric sedan, the fender louvers of the SU7 Ultra Extreme have also changed.
The front bumper carries a larger splitter as well, and Xiaomi appears to have revised the front intakes a bit as well. Along the sides, the Chinese manufacturer I still associate with smartphones and dashcams used larger side skirts to better control airflow. Underbody changes may be featured as well, but these photos don't confirm anything in this regard.
Turning our attention back to the rear end once again, the ginormous rear wing is joined by a new diffuser. From a visual standpoint, it's hard not to make the assumption that Xiaomi took inspiration from Manthey Racing's aerodynamic diffuser for the Porsche Taycan Turbo GT with the Weissach Package.
Another interesting observation concerns the brakes, which are visibly scorching hot in some pictures. The red glow pretty much confirms the carbon-ceramic route to performance braking, and the glow further shows how hard the braking system has to work on a heavy electric vehicle designed with track duty in mind.
Photo: Baldauf Considering that downforce loads both the front and rear suspension, Xiaomi may have worked its magic in this area too, recalibrating the zero-emission bruiser in accordance with this aerodynamic package. The current SU7 Ultra is plenty extreme as is, with Xiaomi claiming 1,548 ps (1,527 hp) from three motors.
Listed with a tremendous amount of peak torque, SU7 Ultra needs 1.98 seconds to reach 100 kilometers per hour (62 miles per hour). It tops out at 350 kilometers per hour (217 miles per hour), making it one of the fastest series-production cars ever. For a company that revealed its first production vehicle (that being the SU7) less than three years ago, those numbers are mighty impressive.
350 clicks explain why the more serious aero matters. A large wing becomes a substantial drag penalty at speed if not gifted with a drag reduction system, and this kind of drag would hurt the Extreme in many corners of the Green Hell. With DRS, the SU7 Ultra Extreme would also make the most out of its powertrain on long straights.
In pre-production form, the SU7 Ultra lapped the German circuit in 6:22 as opposed to 7:04 for the production version. That puts the SU7 Ultra in the crosshairs of the Manthey Racing-prepped Taycan Turbo GT Weissach, and the Extreme will definitely put the Porker to shame.

Dubai Police Expands Exotic Cop Car Lineup With New Lamborghini Temerario
8 photos
Photo: Dubai Police
The Lamborghini Temerario has already established itself as being a great supercar from the modern era. In fact, it is so fantastic that it has become a police car.
The plug-in hybrid exotic model has officially joined Dubai’s police fleet. The local force recently announced that the Temerario has entered its portfolio, which comprises numerous high-end models, some of which are on the very rare side of things. The vehicle has been introduced in partnership with Lamborghini Abu Dhabi and Dubai, and it will take on the usual tourist policing duties and engagement with residents and visitors.
“ Our luxury patrol fleet represents an innovative approach to policing, combining an effective security presence with community and tourist engagement, ” said the Director of the General Department of Criminal Investigation at Dubai Police, Brigadier Saeed Al Hajri. “ These vehicles help people feel safe, showcase Dubai’s positive image to visitors from around the world, and raise awareness of police services and public safety. Above all, they reinforce our commitment to being a police force that is close to the community. ”
Dubai’s police dropped shared an image in the press release that reveals the Lamborghini Temerario dressed in the usual attire. It combines white and green in a distinctive pattern, and also features a pair of emergency lights at the top part of the front windscreen. We reckon additional modifications could be on deck to better help the plug-in hybrid supercar with its new role, though that’s our two cents, and should be taken with the proverbial pinch of salt.
Photo: Lamborghini It is worth reminding ourselves that the Dubai police fleet is constantly growing with all kinds of exotic models. Over the years, we have seen the Bugatti Veyron, Ferrari FF, Lamborghini Aventador, Porsche 918 Spyder, Brabus Mercedes G 63, Lotus Eletre, Mercedes- AMG GT 63 S, a few Mansory-tuned vehicles, including the Ferrari Purosangue and Lmborghini Revuelto, and others. And it looks like there is also a Tesla Cybertruck that wears the same livery.
Mind you, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) is not the only country to have such a cop car, because the Lamborghini Temerario has also joined Italy’s state police department. The announcement was made a little over a month ago, at the beginning of September, 2026, and that ride will be used for “ the most important services, ” according to the local authorities, which include “the emergency transport of organs and medical supplies.”
In this case, Italy’s Lamborghini Temerario cop car features a white and blue livery, and it is decorated with the Italian flag on certain elements. It also features an emergency light bar on the roof, and likely other elements that we are unaware of. And in both cases, there are no mechanical upgrades, because the supercars that have joined Italy’s and the UAE’s police fleets retain their stock firepower.
What does that mean? Well, no fewer than three electric motors assisting the twin-turbocharged V8 engine, which has a 4.0-liter displacement. The ICE alone pumps out 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) between 9,000 and 9,750 rpm. In total, the supercar boasts 907 brake horsepower (920 ps/677 kW) and 538 pound-feet (730 Nm) of torque. It features an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, all-wheel drive, and a lithium-ion battery pack.
Photo: Lamborghini Lamborghini’s Temerario takes a mere 2.7 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from a standstill, the model’s spec sheet reveals, and can keep pushing all the way up to 213 mph (343 kph). It also has a tiny electric range of a few miles for short driving in the zero-emission mode. For the 2027 model year, you are looking at just under $400,000 for a brand new example in the United States of America, and that makes it over $200,000 more affordable than its bigger, punchier, and faster sibling, the Revuelto.
The Lamborghini Temerario was unveiled during the 2024 Monterey Car Week, and it hit the assembly line the following year at the Sant’Agata Bolognese factory. The model replaced the Huracan in the Raging Bull’s exotic car lineup, and it is now the brand’s new “baby” supercar. The same underpinnings have been used for the Audi Nuvolari, which is limited to 499 units, and will hit production toward the end of this year, featuring a very quirky design.
So far, the Lamborghini Temerario family comprises a single member, the one that we have dedicated numerous stories to. However, a Spyder , which is Lambo slang for convertible, is being developed as we speak, and will rock the same hardware, though due to the added weight, it should be a tiny bit slower than its fixed-roof sibling.
The Lamborghini Temerario Spyder is expected to debut in late 2026 or early 2027, and further down the line, the company will keep expanding the lineup with all sort of different versions, which are expected to become faster and faster with each one. After all, its predecessor, the Huracan , came in various variants over the years.

1961 Lincoln Continental Snowblind Goes Full Custom, Yet Keeps Basic Looks and Suicide Doors
6 photos
Photo: Barrett-Jackson
There are still close to three months left in the year, but car collectors are already looking ahead to the many auctions that will be held in the first month of next year, expecting the right car that makes them tingle to come along. For some, that car could be this here 1961 Lincoln Continental.
The Ford brand used the Continental name a number of times during its existence, but for those with a passion for classic and custom vehicles, the defining rides called this way are the ones of the 1960s.
That’s when the brand introduced serious design changes that abandoned the flashy colors and materials and pointy bodywork from before, and went for cleaner, almost sombre lines that allowed the incorporation of suicide doors.
These changes are, more or less, what keeps the 1960s Continentals in the news in our day and time, and make them the focus of custom shops across America, which remake them in any way imaginable and then sell them for a lot of money.
The particular 1961 Continental we have here is the work of an unnamed such garage, and it is now in the news because it’s getting ready to sell during the Barrett-Jackson auction in early January 2027.
The custom and collector world knows this vehicle as the Snowblind, and in time it has earned a number of recognitions and awards, including the First Class win at this year’s Grand National Roadster Show in Pomona, California.
The build is based on the Continental that first introduced the suicide doors and, naturally, retained those. It also retained most of its original lines and design cues, but underneath all that old-school looks, a world of wonders hides.
The Continental’s chassis is supported by a custom setup that includes a four-link arrangement with coilovers. Stopping power is supplied by Baer disc brakes with an electric hydro-boost system. To move around, the car offers Flaming River rack-and-pinion steering.
Steering would be useless if it weren’t for a powertrain to get the car going. In this case, the long metal hood of the Continental hides an LS3 engine built by Southern Performance, paired to a 4L70E automatic transmission and a Ford 9-inch rear end with 3.70 gears and 31-spline axles.
It’s not clear exactly how much power the engine on the convertible cranks out, but that’s probably enough to satisfy needs and desires. The dual-fan aluminum radiator and Devious Customs aluminum fuel tank are some of the indications of its capabilities.
The bodywork of the Continental comes in Pearl White and is propped on Isotope wheels of undisclosed dimensions, while wearing a new canvas top. Inside, there are four bucket seats wrapped in leather, Dakota Digital gauges in the dashboard, and hardware that allows Bluetooth connectivity.
With just 460 miles (740 km) on the odometer since being remade, the Continental will sell in Arizona in January with no reserve, meaning that whoever offers the most for it will get it.

2027 Chevrolet Colorado Order Guide Confirms ZR2 Desert Boss Edition's Return
7 photos
Photo: Chevrolet / edited
The Desert Boss story continues for 2027, with Chevrolet indirectly confirming the return of the off-road package through the order guide for the Colorado. Listed under regular production option code PDK, the dealer-installed limited production option is exclusive to the ZR2 model.
Highlights include Multimatic jounce control dampers, auxiliary lighting, a purposeful front bumper, Tech Bronze-finished recovery hooks, door sill plates, and fender decals. The most important of highlights obviously comes in the form of the Multimatic-supplied dampers, which feature nitrogen-charged hydraulic bump stops.
Those bump stops are designed to prevent bottoming out during extreme off-road impacts. Unlike stops that simply cushion the final inch of suspension travel, hydraulic bump stops rely on nitrogen gas and hydraulic oil to progressively absorb kinetic energy. This hardware is also featured on the ZR2 Bison , which indirectly replaced the original Desert Boss.
By offering these dampers on the ZR2 Desert Boss Edition for 2027, the Chevrolet division gives prospective customers a way to add the Bison's biggest differentiator without being forced to buy the complementary American Expedition Vehicles equipment. Said overlap also explains two exclusions listed in the 2027 model year Colorado order guide.
As it happens, the Desert Boss treatment cannot be combined with the Bison (RPO code ULV) or the Midnight Edition (RPO code WJP). The Bison already has those clever dampers, and the Midnight Edition's visuals would clash with the Desert Boss graphics, lighting, and bronze recovery hooks.
Photo: Chevrolet Colorado ZR2 Desert Boss Edition customers are presented with the BPH off-road front bumper package and the PCL off-road lighting package, but alas, the newcomer is a bit leaner than what Chevrolet used to sell originally. As a brief refresher, the previous model used to ship with a bed-mounted sport bar, a safari bar up front, beadlock-capable wheels, roof-mounted auxiliary lighting, an underbody camera system, and unique graphics.
The Multimatic dampers shift the Desert Boss from a visual and accessory bundle toward a more focused suspension upgrade, and that matters a lot more off the beaten path. Instead of looking ready for Baja, the new one promises to be more composed when its suspension runs out of travel. Customers who fancy the old beadlock wheels or sport bar will have to look elsewhere.
All Colorados feature a familiar 8-speed automatic transmission, but under the hood, things have changed this model year. Known as L4B, the 2.7-liter turbo inline-four gasoline mill that replaces the L3B puts out 350 horsepower and 450 pound-feet (610 Newton-meters) of torque.
Production should kick off later this month, with all Colorados hailing from the Wentzville plant in the state of Missouri. As ever, the Colorado range splits into the WT, LT, Trail Boss, Z71, and ZR2.
Pricing for 2027 has yet to be finalized. Until Chevy updates the configurator, it's worth keeping in mind that $32,400 from the outset makes the 2026 model year Colorado one of the most affordable midsizers out there.
